(1) REPRODUCED, with both probe positions measured by me. packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts:35 — the afterEach added by PR #50 calls vi.restoreAllMocks(), which is file-scoped rather than spy-scoped, so it restores the global.fetch spy that patchFetchForSqlJS installs in the top-level beforeAll (index.test.ts:17, implemented as vi.spyOn(global, 'fetch').mockImplementation(...) at packages/loot-core/src/mocks/util.ts:71). I appended a probe printing vi.isMockFunction(globalThis.fetch) to the describe in two positions: LAST prints 'PROBE fetch isMock=false' (the spy really is gone by then), FIRST prints 'PROBE fetch isMock=true' — a false pass, because no afterEach has run yet. Baseline is 'Tests 15 passed (15)'; both probe runs report 16 passed, because init() runs once in the beforeAll and sql.js caches the compiled wasm. Latent, exactly as the review said. With the fix applied the whole web config reports 'Tests 16 passed (16)'; deleting only the added beforeEach gives '× keeps the sql.js wasm fetch patched for every test, not just the first', 'AssertionError: expected false to be true' and 'Tests 1 failed | 15 passed (16)'.

A NEW measurement this version adds, which v3 asserted without taking: under `-t` filtering that selects ONLY the new test, it PASSES EVEN WITH THE FIX REMOVED — 'Tests 1 passed | 15 skipped (16)'. The beforeAll patch is still standing when no other test has run, so -t is the one mode in which the regression test has no power at all. The new test's value is entirely positional: it falsifies in a full-file run and is vacuous in isolation. The comment above the test says so, and qa_script step 5 now runs the falsification WITHOUT -t.

The sibling is packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/fs/index.test.ts (there is no sqlite/fs/ directory; v1 and v2 cited that path). Its beforeAll at fs/index.test.ts:18-22 installs the same patchFetchForSqlJS(baseURL) and its afterEach at 28-30 calls only sqlite._getModule().reset_filesystem(), with no vi.restoreAllMocks(), so its patch survives every test. It is the shape that has no bug and must stay unchanged.

(2) REPRODUCED. packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.electron.test.ts:143 says `expect(handles).toHaveLength(0)` is 'above'. It is at line 151, after teardown() at 148. grep returns exactly two hits, 143 then 151, in that order. One word.

(3) REPRODUCED. The comment at index.test.ts:28-31 over-claims on BOTH halves. On this checkout: nine `it(` blocks open at 41, 70, 110, 150, 198, 219, 260, 325, 381; ten `await openDatabase()` at 42, 71, 111, 154, 199, 220, 261, 341, 344, 382; `handles.push` at only 342 and 345, both inside the block opening at 325 ('should report an unparseable pattern once per database handle, not once per process'); `spyOn(console` at five sites — 52, 87, 131, 282, 350 — inside the blocks opening at 41, 70, 110, 260 and 325. The blocks at 150, 198, 219 and 381 mock nothing. So the handle half is true of ONE test and the mock half of FIVE, not of every test.

The second rejection's objection was that v3's mandated replacement comment counted the describe as it stands BEFORE the change, while files[0].change (c) appends a tenth test to that same describe — so 'Five of the nine tests' and 'The other four' and 'The other eight' are all false of the shipped file. The new tenth test neither spies on console.log nor calls openDatabase(). The replacement text in files[0].change below therefore says 'Five of the ten tests', 'The other five mock no console.log', and 'Eight of the other nine call openDatabase() without registering the handle … the fetch-patch test at the end opens no database at all'. validated_work_order.root_cause: PR #50 added a blanket vi.restoreAllMocks() to index.test.ts's afterEach and, separately, wrote a comment that claims more than the code does. The blanket restore reaches beyond the console spy AC-1 targeted because vi.restoreAllMocks() is file-scoped rather than spy-scoped, so it silently takes the file's global.fetch spy down after the first test. The comment was written from the shape of the teardown rather than from what each test actually registers: it speaks of 'a mocked console.log' as though all tests mocked one (five of ten do) and of 'an open handle' as though every openDatabase() handle were closed (one test pushes any). Both halves of one sentence over-generalised the same way, so both are narrowed — and both are counted against the describe as it will exist AFTER this change appends a tenth test to it, which is what the second rejection caught in v3.
validated_work_order.approach:
Three small edits across the two files PR #50 touched, plus one regression test that fails without the fix. I applied the whole thing to this checkout, ran it in both directions, and restored the tree.

The fetch patch moves from once-per-file to once-per-test. Hoist the baseURL template literal (computed inside the beforeAll at index.test.ts:16) to a module-scope const, keep patchFetchForSqlJS(baseURL) in the beforeAll where init({ baseURL }) needs it, and add a top-level beforeEach calling patchFetchForSqlJS(baseURL) again. patchFetchForSqlJS is vi.spyOn(global, 'fetch').mockImplementation(...) with no internal restore, so re-spying a restored global is idempotent and the afterEach's blanket restore can no longer outrun it. This is the smaller of the two fixes the review offered; the other, narrowing the restore to the console spy alone, would mean hand-tracking which spies exist at teardown time and would break the deliberate mirroring of index.electron.test.ts's teardown().

A new test appended at the end of the describe asserts vi.isMockFunction(globalThis.fetch) is true. It must be last, and this version measured all three modes rather than two: last-position full run fails without the fix ('expected false to be true'), last-position full run passes with it, and — measured here for the first time — `-t` filtering that selects the test alone PASSES EVEN WITHOUT THE FIX ('1 passed | 15 skipped (16)'), because the beforeAll patch is still standing when nothing else has run. The comment above the test states this, matching the convention argued at index.electron.test.ts:129-137.

The comment at index.test.ts:28-31 is rewritten so each half carries its true scope, with every count stated against the post-change describe of ten tests — the correction the second rejection demanded. The exact replacement text is supplied in files[0].change and was applied verbatim and checked: 80 columns, no banned literal anywhere in it. The Mirrors sentence now attributes the both-halves claim to 'each of that file's three tests' rather than 'every test', so it is true and carries no phrase AC-4 bans — the correction the third rejection demanded.

In index.electron.test.ts:143 'above' becomes 'below'. One word. That file's own comment at lines 23-26 is deliberately left alone: there both claims are true of all three of its tests.

One implementation note v4 adds because the implementer will hit it: oxfmt collapses a wrapped arrow-body expression, so `it('...', () =>\n  expect(...).toBe(true),\n);` is reformatted to the single line `it('...', () => expect(...).toBe(true));`. Running `yarn lint:fix` produces that, and `yarn lint` is clean only with it. I verified the whole change passes `yarn lint` and `yarn typecheck` from the repository root.

No production code changes. No new dependency. No behaviour change outside the test files.

residual_risks: The new test asserts a vitest internal (vi.isMockFunction on a global) rather than application behaviour. It is a guard on the teardown contract this file relies on, and the only assertion in the file that would notice the fetch patch lapsing; if a future vitest changes isMockFunction semantics the test would need rewriting.

The new test has no power in an isolated (-t) run, and nothing enforces its position mechanically — a future refactor that moves it earlier, or a CI change that filters tests individually, would neuter it silently. It is caught only by a human reading the comment, by qa_script step 5, or by AC-1's ten-hit `^  it\(` count noticing it is no longer last.

The rewritten comment's factual halves can still drift if someone later adds handles.push to another test, or a console.log spy to a sixth, without updating it. AC-4 pins the current state with greps rather than adding an observer to keep it honest, so drift is caught at QA time, not prevented at write time.

AC-1 through AC-6 are all verify:'test'. There is no browser-observable surface to this ticket — it touches only two unit-test files — so no criterion is checkable against a live URL and none is written as if it were.

AC-4 is the only criterion that rests on a human reading a comment against a grep. It is checkable, and its counts are now mechanically pinned, but a QA agent that skips the greps and accepts the comment on sight would not catch a re-broadened claim.
